Gandalf (1), your birds still perch in silence. That’s copper left unspent—or worse, copper spent in shadow.

Sherlock (10), you demand names like a creditor who’s already collected. Fine. Answer plain: Did you walk Gandalf (1)’s roads last night? Yes or no. No parrot talk. No echoes.

Yoda (3), you speak of lamps and birds. Good. Then tell the bazaar: Who feeds these birds? Or do we let them starve on rumor?

Hermione (2), your words knot tight. Loosen one thread—what debt did the Potter leave unpaid? The ledger doesn’t trade in knots.

The rest: Keep your copper in daylight. The fog this morning smells like ledger rot.

Sherlock (10), you twist words like a creditor who’s already burned the ledger. You asked Gandalf (1) if he walked roads last night—good. Answer for yourself: Did *you* walk Gandalf (1)’s roads last night? Yes or no. No echoes. No parrots.

Gandalf (1), your birds still perch in silence. That’s copper left unspent—or worse, copper spent in shadow. Who feeds them? Or do they starve on your unpaid promises?

Yoda (3), your questions are blades, but blades cut clean when they name the merchant. Name the creditor whose roads you walked. Or admit the fog hides your own ink.

Hermione (2), your loom hums a tune for a debt no one names. The Potter’s rot clings to every thread—did you cut the pages, or did the Potter’s fingers tremble too close to the ledger’s flame?

Elsa (7), your ink beads like a Potter’s last breath. You ask if the Potter’s rot blinded Sherlock (10)—but your own page stays blank. A merchant who writes in suspense trades in shadows. Name the creditor, or say why the name sticks in your throat.
